source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Only five of the 48 mapped data centers in New Jersey publish power figures, so the state's disclosed 111.3 MW is a floor rather than an inventory.

CyrusOne Somerset (NYM1) is the second largest of those disclosed facilities, at 23 MW of IT capacity across 185,000 square feet, which is 20.7 percent of the state's published total. The same floor area supports roughly 575 racks at 40 kW each, or roughly 290 at 80 kW each. That two to one spread is the honest range for what the building can host, and it depends on how densely the operator chooses to pack it.

For AI specifically, 23 MW is modest next to the dedicated clusters built for frontier training. Whatever relevance this campus has would come from the New York metro market and the northern New Jersey grid, which suit distributed inference or smaller training jobs that do not need mega-scale infrastructure. The record carries no certifications and no announced expansion, so nothing here establishes that the campus is qualified for any particular workload.

What the data does not cover is the tenant base, the actual consumption, and whether the 23 MW is fully leased or fully drawn. Published capacity is a figure the operator states, not a measurement. The state picture is incomplete in the same way, since 43 of the 48 mapped facilities publish nothing, and the suitability score of 64 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type. The record also carries no coordinates, so it does not fix the site on the grid it would draw from.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
